## 固定收益開篇論點

8月12日美國固定收益市場收盤僅將溫和的7月CPI報告轉化為政策敏感區段的小幅上漲，長端仍受財政供給帶來的存續期間風險與尚未解除的能源衝擊壓制。2年期美國公債殖利率下跌2個基點至4.20%，5年期回落1個基點至4.38%，10年期下降2個基點至4.68%，30年期則持平於5.24%。相較於CPI公布前的收盤水準，這份數據支持Fed耐心觀望，卻未為政策轉鬆打開空間：市場對9月升息的定價由約50%降至約40%，但年底前升息仍已完全反映在價格中。

7月通膨足以降低政策急迫性，卻不足以釐清反應函數。整體CPI月增0.1%、年增3.4%，均符合市場共識，年增率並由3.5%回落。核心CPI月增0.2%，同樣符合共識，年增率則由2.6%降至2.5%。住房項目漲幅溫和、能源價格下跌，但租金持續上升，科技相關商品價格也加速上漲。10年期名目公債上漲由兩項因素平均貢獻：實質殖利率下降1個基點至2.42%，損益兩平通膨率亦回落1個基點至2.26%；這是有節制的反應，而非通膨風險的全面重定價。

供給面使這波利多未能延伸至整條殖利率曲線。$420億10年期美國公債標售的得標殖利率為4.683%，創2007年以來新高，且略高於標售前的市場水準。2s10s曲線維持在48個基點，但因長債未跟漲，2s30s曲線陡峭化2個基點至104個基點。拉長至1個月觀察，2年期殖利率下降1個基點，10年期與30年期殖利率卻分別上升12及18個基點。CPI改變了近期政策時點的討論，卻未消除市場針對實質利率、赤字與買方基礎風險所要求的補償。

能源仍是主要的反向力量。WTI與Brent當日分別下跌0.90%與0.66%，但1週漲幅仍達9.61%與11.16%；國際能源總署估計，本季每日供給缺口達180萬桶，是先前預估的2倍以上。儘管如此，風險資產仍將CPI視為擴大成長曝險的許可，信用市場則同時呈現融資管道普遍暢通與個別發行人嚴重分化。Jane Street發行$146億擔保債券，但Air Baltic與The Knot顯示，高融資成本與疲弱商業模式能多快侵蝕債權人價值。因此，本次收盤較適合作狹義解讀：Fed近期壓力減輕，但長存續期間資產與財務體質較弱的發行人，仍暴露於油價、供給與再融資風險。

## 美國公債利率、Fed定價、實質殖利率與曲線結構

利率變動集中在政策敏感與中段券種，但幅度不大本身就很重要。2年期殖利率報4.20%，已回到接近8月7日非農就業報告公布後的水準；然而5年期4.38%與10年期4.68%仍高於當日收盤，30年期債券更完全未上漲。這只是7月非農就業人數減少23,000人、此前2個月合計下修103,000人所開啟的前端喘息獲得確認，並不代表疲弱勞動市場已取代通膨與供給，成為制約長端的主導因素。

CPI組成讓主張耐心觀望的官員有充分理由繼續等待。整體通膨繼6月下降0.4%後，7月回升0.1%，3.4%的年增率則放緩0.1個百分點。核心通膨月增率由0.0%升至0.2%，完全符合共識；核心年增率降至2.5%，同樣符合預期，並追平2021年3月以來最低增速。能源價格下跌1.5%，住房項目僅上升0.1%，約占整體CPI單月增幅的三分之二。旅館與汽車旅館價格下跌有助抑制住房項目，但兩項主要租金指標仍均上升0.3%。

底層價格漲勢的廣度令人稍感安心，但各類別並非全面疲弱。扣除能源與租金的服務價格在6月下降後上升0.2%，醫療照護與機票價格均列入上漲項目。扣除食品與能源的商品價格則在連續2個月下跌後反彈。電腦軟體與配件較去年同期上漲21.2%，創歷來最大增幅；記憶體晶片短缺與資料中心擴建，也推動其他電腦相關類別錄得逾4年來最強漲幅。這些局部壓力不會推翻整體通膨降溫，但也限制了市場據此認定單月溫和數據已消除本土生成或科技相關價格壓力的空間。

家戶所得為成長前景增添一項限制條件。7月實質平均時薪較去年同期下降0.2%，延續伊朗衝突爆發以來的疲弱表現。這有助解釋，為何同一份CPI報告即使顯示整體通膨仍遠高於2%，仍能降低立即緊縮的風險：實質薪資並未轉強，購買力因此沒有進一步放大價格衝擊。Fed可將這項疲弱與招聘降溫一併衡量，但7月會議出現3票反對，加上租金仍具黏性，後續數據必須證明市場目前定價的年底升息可以取消，而不只是延後。

通膨連結市場的收盤表現反映了這項平衡。10年期實質殖利率下降1個基點至2.42%，損益兩平通膨率也回落1個基點至2.26%。拉長至1個月，實質殖利率上升10個基點，損益兩平通膨率僅上升2個基點，顯示累積壓力仍主要來自偏高的實質資金成本與存續期間不確定性。當日名目殖利率的下滑由實質殖利率與通膨補償平均貢獻，與前一交易日由損益兩平通膨率主導的債市上漲，以及週一由能源帶動的損益兩平通膨率擴大形成對比。投資人接受7月CPI並未再度加速，但仍要求偏高的實質殖利率門檻，對油價風險也只打了部分折扣。

曲線結構清楚區分了政策時點與期限溢價。2年期與10年期殖利率均下跌2個基點，2s10s斜率因此持平於48個基點。30年期殖利率持穩，則使2s30s斜率擴大至104個基點。拉長至1個月，兩條曲線分別陡峭化13及19個基點。當日前端的小幅變動不像市場全面撤回緊縮預期，更像不確定性由9月移向後續會議；財政與通膨溢價則隨到期年限拉長而持續累積。

10年期標售為這項差異確立了市場出清價格。$420億發售的得標殖利率為4.683%，創金融危機以來新高，並略高於投標前一刻的水準。需求足以避免失序的新券讓利，卻不足以將一份溫和CPI轉化為基準公債的持續上漲。偏高的標售殖利率可以吸引資金參與，同時仍顯示投資人要求主權借款人付出異常昂貴的融資條件。10年期結果不能自動推論至下一個標售年期；再融資日程上的每個年期，都承受不同的存續期間與買方基礎負擔。

現券交易顯示，有限的收盤變動發生在大量風險移轉之中。名目息票券交易以原始面額計達$9,461億，較前一交易日增加19.7%。2年期以下券種的交易量增加33.4%，7至10年期區段增加30.9%；這兩個區域最直接承受CPI重定價與標售影響。這些總量無法辨識客戶交易方向，卻證明殖利率僅小幅變動並非市場清淡所造成的假象。政策利多與供給承接能力都經過大額交易檢驗，市場收盤時長端仍不願跟漲。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

信用資產跟隨利率債上漲，卻未出現全面的風險重定價。LQD上漲0.12%、HYG上升0.13%、JNK上漲0.17%。這些是與美國公債殖利率小幅下降及風險偏好穩健一致的總報酬漲幅，並非現券利差收窄的衡量指標。更具訊息含量的分野，在於能以偏高絕對票息換取大額融資的借款人，以及必須在保護債權人的條款下尋求延長到期日的弱勢企業。初級市場融資管道仍普遍暢通，但成本與損失分配高度取決於擔保品、業務耐久性與槓桿。

Jane Street提供了最明確的承接結果。這家造市商發行$146億優先擔保票據：$58.6億於2031年到期、$51.3億於2033年到期，另有$36.4億於2036年到期。最長年期券種的殖利率為8.088%。資金將用於一項$110億債務重整，以再融資浮動利率貸款，並支應科技基礎設施與交易策略擴張。這筆交易將一項大型私人融資安排轉化為固定利率公開債務，但即使前一年度交易收入創下$396億紀錄，該殖利率仍揭示取得如此融資能力所需付出的價格。

評級反映獲利能力強勁與資產負債表不透明並存的不尋常組合。S&P給予債券BB評級，較投資等級低2級；Fitch的發行人評級則為BBB-，是投資等級最低一級。擔保地位與公司的獲利能力支撐了異常龐大的發行規模，但投資人對10年期曝險仍要求8%字頭的殖利率。這項結果證明，市場願意為具策略重要性的科技支出與再融資提供資金；同時也顯示，大額融資管道不應與低廉資金混為一談，尤其當一家股權高度集中的借款人正透過公開市場提高槓桿透明度之際。

資料中心融資仍是另一個集中供給來源。QTS子公司已針對一筆潛在發行展開固定收益投資人電話會議，規模約$28.5億且可能增加，預計取得投資等級評級。這筆融資與Blackstone支持、出租給Microsoft的喬治亞州開發案有關；此前市場曾討論一套可能達$54億的債券與貸款組合，7月另有以Project Magnolia為擔保的$32.5億槓桿貸款。目前階段是接觸投資人，並非已完成發售。其重要性在於，專案、企業與資產擔保等管道正迅速且反覆地用來為同一波基礎設施擴建提供資金。

Shanghai Electric展現了另一種市場重啟形式。這家市政府支持的設備製造商在上海自由貿易區發行人民幣15億元3年期綠色票據，定價1.8%，初步討論水準則約2.4%。這是當局於2023年底限制地方政府舉債後，首家在該市場完成定價的非金融企業，也是發行人自2020年以來首次境外發債。香港子公司擔保、維好協議與A3評級共同促使殖利率收窄。這筆交易為品質較高的發行人重啟受控的離岸人民幣融資管道，同時保留對先前促使監管收緊之槓桿行為的限制。

在壓力端，The Knot的修約展期方案顯示，再融資能力已同時取決於價格與槓桿保護。公司推出$6.7億貸款，計畫將現有$6.6億融資延長2.5年；就在數小時前，Moody's才將其評級下調2級至Caa1。擬議利差為基準利率加525個基點，高於原先的375個基點；若槓桿達到至少4倍EBITDA，還將再加100個基點，且這部分可採PIK支付。現有貸款價格已由去年底約99美分跌至約70美分。

The Knot的營運惡化說明了條件為何如此嚴苛。營收在2025年下降2%，預計2026年將再度下滑；隨著AI生成式搜尋減少流量與供應商互動，利潤率仍將停留在20%出頭。S&P維持B評級，但指出槓桿若高於獲利的7倍，將構成降評風險。因此，這筆融資只是延長時間，並未恢復原有信用體質。槓桿升高時使用PIK可保護近期現金，卻可能在其平台逐漸失去市場重要性之際，進一步增加最終債務負擔。

Air Baltic則顯示價值移轉已進入更後期。其€3.8億、2029年到期的優先擔保票據，在重整公告前約為每1歐元35歐分，之後一度跌至12歐分；不過這檔交易清淡的債券也曾報在20歐分出頭。航空公司計畫將大部分票據轉為股權，讓債券持有人保留€1.25億債務，另籌集€2.25億過渡融資，同時縮減機隊與成本。截至6月，償債準備金僅有€300萬。拉脫維亞持有88.4%股權與13%債券，但國家持股仍未能避免擔保債權人蒙受重大減損。

綜合來看，這些案例描繪出運作正常、但分層極為鮮明的承接市場。Jane Street以異常高的殖利率取得異常大的規模；QTS正測試市場能否反覆吸收基礎設施融資；Shanghai Electric則在強力結構性支持下重啟受監管的融資管道。The Knot與Air Baltic透過更高利差、PIK選項、債轉股與稀釋，付出代價以換取時間。整體報酬溫和仍可與這種分化共存，因為市場依然提供資本。真正的分界，在於新增資金是支應可持續現金流與擔保品，還是只把資本結構的最終清算往後推延。

## 全球存續期間風險、央行與財政傳導

海外長天期債券未同步呼應美國通膨降溫所帶來的利多。日本與韓國反而顯示，即使美國公債前端壓力減輕，能源曝險、國內政策與買方行為仍可使長端殖利率維持高檔。對美國長存續期間債券的直接意涵是競爭，而非傳染：較高的本地殖利率為國內機構提供美元債券以外的選擇，匯率防衛也可能改變外匯存底管理誘因；通膨結果分歧，則使全球政策無法走上共同路徑。

日本目前的變化，政治與貨幣因素同樣重要。美國財政部長Scott Bessent一再將日本央行收緊政策視為穩定日圓的核心，首相Sanae Takaichi則不願因行動過快而犧牲成長。Takaichi上任後，日本央行已升息2次，但政策利率仍為1%，且在美日聯手干預日圓當天維持利率不變。日圓再度逼近1美元兌160日圓；若貨幣政策與官方訊號無法指向同一方向，干預效果將持續減弱。

市場預期日本央行可能在9月或10月升息，反映的正是這項限制，但政府的容忍度仍有條件。隨著生活成本問題更受關注，Takaichi的支持度已經下滑；日本央行官員強調通膨上行風險，內閣成員也持續支持央行獨立性。Bessent預計在8月底前後與日本央行總裁Kazuo Ueda會面。政策立場若更趨一致，可降低反覆干預匯市的必要；若歧見持續，日本仍可能必須結合更高的本地殖利率與更積極的外匯存底管理，進一步提高美國公債的相對價值門檻。

韓國則提供了已實現的長端壓力訊號。30年期政府公債殖利率升至4.67%，創2012年推出該年期以來新高。進口能源成本偏高，加上韓國央行一名高階官員警告半導體帶動的成長可能需要進一步緊縮，原已對曲線造成壓力；壽險公司需求疲弱又增添了明確的買方基礎問題。明年超長期公債發行占比可能降至發行計畫的30%以下，最終或可改變供給結構；但目前的紀錄高殖利率顯示，通膨與結構性需求不足現階段須以更高殖利率才能完成市場出清。

油價衝擊的影響也超出央行利率。國際能源總署目前估計，本季全球供給缺口為每日180萬桶，是先前預估的2倍以上，且各方尚未就荷姆茲海峽達成可持續的協議。歐洲電價還面臨高溫推升冷房需求，以及法國核能發電受限的額外壓力。在一項附帶條件的最壞情境中，若荷姆茲海峽至年底仍實質封閉，英國財政部內部模型估計2026年經濟成長率為0.9%，低於3月公布的1.1%預測。這項情境並非已實現的成長結果，卻捕捉到停滯性通膨的財政風險：經濟活動轉弱與能源成本上升可以同時發生。

對美國公債的淨傳導仍不對稱。美國CPI降溫可降低Fed立即行動的機率，但日本政策不確定性、韓國長端殖利率創高，以及全球能源缺口擴大，仍支撐期限溢價。部分經濟體的通膨降溫可能有利於當地前端，但策略性美元長存續期間需求仍須與更高的本地市場殖利率及匯率管理需求競爭。因此，面對單一一份有利的通膨數據，美國長端的反應仍不如政策敏感區段。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

新興市場資產並未從CPI獲得明確的共同因子利多。美元指數在扭轉早盤跌勢後，上漲0.11%至99.932；一項新興市場貨幣指標則吐回盤中最多0.2%的漲幅，紐約收盤近乎持平。EMB上漲0.12%，長存續期間新興市場美元主權債指數僅升0.04%。這項組合不支持美元流動性緊縮的判斷，但也顯示，9月升息機率下降仍不足以壓過油價曝險與各地政治風險。

貨幣分化點出了真正的斷層。受貴金屬支撐，南非蘭特上漲近0.3%；巴西里亞爾下跌0.3%，韓元也貶值0.4%。隨著選舉風險進入定價，里亞爾8月以來已下跌近2%；韓元則反映進口能源成本，以及韓國政府公債同樣可見的長端壓力。這些走勢發生在新興市場股票上漲之際，因此差異並非來自一般性的風險偏好，而是商品曝險、國內政策公信力與預期財政供給的分布不同。

印尼位於相對具韌性的一端，儘管修復仍未完成。在民粹支出、央行獨立性與政府干預的疑慮推動印尼盾跌至歷史低點後，以美元計價的投資人今年持有印尼債券仍虧損8.5%，為亞洲最差表現。Destry Damayanti獲提名出任印尼央行總裁，已恢復部分政策延續性；政府也計畫縮減免費供餐方案，並維持今年公債淨發行目標。S&P確認主權評級與展望，進一步提供制度面支撐。

市場反應可以量化。印尼基準10年期公債殖利率已較2022年以來最高點下滑約27個基點；最近一次債券標售的投標金額相對目標發行額之比創2月以來最高，外資也可望連續第3個月淨流入。這些事實顯示，政策穩定正吸引資金回流，但財政疑問尚未消失。下年度預算的公信力，以及央行能否在不犧牲自身職責下支撐匯率，仍是區分持久正常化與另一次油價敏感型反轉的關鍵條件。

巴西則位於脆弱的一端，儘管里亞爾以全年計仍是新興市場表現最強的貨幣之一。在極高實質利率支撐下，里亞爾2026年迄今仍升值約6%；但選舉避險部位仍少，本地公債殖利率上升，每週財政部標售的需求也轉弱。通膨連結政府公債的實質殖利率已升破8%。這種組合使主權資產負債表承擔利差交易的代價異常高昂；若投資人在10月總統大選前要求避險，匯率也將承受壓力。

新增風險不只在於最終勝選者是誰。民調顯示總統Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva的領先擴大，再度引發市場質疑下一屆政府能否創造足以穩定債務的基本盈餘。本地資產管理人以短端利率下降、長端利率上升的預期表達這項擔憂，曲線反映貨幣寬鬆與財政壓力相互碰撞。巴西偏高的名目與實質殖利率可長期吸引資金，但標售需求疲弱顯示，在政治結果揭曉前，對價格敏感的本地買方已開始要求額外補償。

新興市場公司債顯示，主權與企業風險應繼續分開看待。廣泛新興市場美元公司債指數的殖利率在8月已下降19個基點，美國公司債僅下降2個基點，使前者的相對融資成本降至1月以來最低。受惠於荷姆茲海峽封閉的石油生產商，以及重整取得進展的困境借款人領漲。China Vanke的2027年債券在評級上調後，較6月底回報30%；Gran Tierra Energy的2031年票據則上漲18%。這是能源與個別企業復甦交易，而非新興市場全面風險偏好轉強的訊號。

整體結論是，在美元流動性穩定下，市場仍高度分化。印尼透過制度延續、財政節制與標售需求增強重新贏得公信力；巴西則因選舉與債務可持續性風險，正失去部分利差交易溢價；石油相關新興市場企業受惠之際，能源進口國主權債卻面臨更高成本。美國公債小幅上漲對硬通貨資產估值略有幫助，但本地政策與商品衝擊的歸屬，影響仍大於共同的美國利率因子。

## 跨資產

跨資產市場將CPI解讀為近期政策壓力的暫時緩解，而非成長警訊。S&P 500上漲0.26%、Nasdaq 100上升0.74%、半導體類股上漲2.49%，VIX則下跌4.78%至14.55。科技股主導漲勢，與CPI對預期經濟活動影響有限的判斷一致，也反映市場持續看好AI基礎設施。這同時保留Fed耐心觀望所面臨的金融條件反作用力：預期緊縮週期只是延後、並未取消，風險資產卻已走強。

商品市場使這項溫和解讀更為複雜。WTI與Brent在當日小幅下跌後，分別收於$82.45與$88.32；但兩者1週漲幅分別達9.61%與11.16%，顯示實體供給衝擊尚未回歸常態。即使美元指數上升0.11%、10年期實質殖利率僅下降1個基點，黃金仍上漲2.52%至$4,493.60。這項組合顯示，在股市上漲之際，市場對地緣政治與制度性風險的避險需求仍在；這並非Fed定價轉鬆後美元單純走弱的反應。

信用與新興市場資產也呈現相同的混合訊號。投資等級債、高收益債與EMB小幅正報酬，與市場運作有序及基準殖利率下滑一致。新興市場貨幣未能延續漲勢、Air Baltic債券崩跌，以及The Knot承受懲罰性的再融資條件，則顯示充沛的整體風險偏好並未抹平所有資產負債表或政策面的差異。跨資產走勢支持前端僅獲有限喘息的論點；油價、黃金與發行人分化則維持長端與低品質資產仍須具備較高風險溢價的理由。

## 後續市場意涵

8月13日美東時間08:30公布的7月PPI，是檢驗CPI利多能否延伸至核心PCE投入項目的下一關。市場共識預期月增0.2%，前值為月減0.3%，市場也流傳月增0.1%的預測。若結果大致落在這些範圍內，且服務或貿易利潤率未見廣泛壓力，將強化Fed可等待下一份就業與CPI報告的論點，利率反應也將以2至5年期殖利率最為明顯。若結果廣泛高於預期，將暴露7月CPI在多大程度上仰賴能源下跌與暫時性類別疲弱，重新提高市場對9月的敏感度，並使調整同時透過實質殖利率與通膨補償傳導。Kevin Warsh於8月稍後在Jackson Hole的談話，將進一步顯示Fed主席是否認可市場由立即行動轉向延後行動，或刻意保留更寬廣的政策結果區間。

8月13日$250億30年期美國公債標售，必須在CPI降溫但30年期殖利率仍持於5.24%的市場中完成出清。先前10年期標售的得標殖利率為4.683%，略高於標售前水準，因此關鍵觀察包括長債標售結果相對其自身發行前交易殖利率、需求分布，以及分配後次級市場交易是否穩定。非交易商廣泛參與且標售後走勢受控，將顯示即使赤字與海外競爭尚未解決，目前的絕對殖利率仍能吸收存續期間供給。若出現標售尾差、交易商承接比例偏高或曲線再度陡峭化，將強化本月30年期殖利率上升18個基點的走勢，並確認前端政策利多無法取代更高的財政出清價格。

荷姆茲海峽仍是串連美國通膨、全球存續期間與新興市場分化的檢驗。船舶持續通行、各方接受協議條款、運費與保險摩擦下降，加上原油維持在8月12日收盤價以下，將削弱國際能源總署上修後的供給缺口路徑，並減輕損益兩平通膨率、韓國長債與石油進口國主權債所受壓力。若封鎖持續或執法衝突再起，尤其實體流量仍受阻，7月CPI能源價格下降1.5%將只是回顧性的短暫喘息，而非可供政策持續仰賴的依據。若油價再度上漲，且損益兩平通膨率與2年期殖利率同步走高，市場解讀的改變便會浮現；若這條傳導未發生，則顯示市場仍認為衝擊雖然劇烈，廣度卻不足以迫使Fed行動。

overall_summary.headline: CPI降溫緩解Fed近期壓力，長端仍未跟漲

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 12 U.S. fixed-income close converted a benign July CPI report into only a modest policy-sector rally, leaving the long end pinned by fiscal duration and an unresolved energy shock. The 2-year Treasury yield fell 2 basis points to 4.20%, the 5-year eased 1 basis point to 4.38%, and the 10-year declined 2 basis points to 4.68%, while the 30-year held at 5.24%. Relative to the pre-CPI close, the data validated patience at the Federal Reserve without clearing the way for easing: market pricing for a September increase fell to roughly 40% from about 50%, but a move remained fully priced by year-end.

July inflation was soft enough to reduce urgency, not soft enough to resolve the reaction function. Headline CPI rose 0.1% month on month and 3.4% year on year, both matching consensus, with the annual rate down from 3.5%. Core prices increased 0.2% on the month, also matching consensus, and slowed to 2.5% annually from 2.6%. Shelter was subdued and energy fell, yet rents continued to rise and technology-related goods prices accelerated. The 10-year nominal rally split evenly between a 1-basis-point decline in the real yield to 2.42% and a 1-basis-point fall in the breakeven to 2.26%, a measured response rather than a wholesale repricing of inflation risk.

Supply kept that relief from extending through the curve. The $42 billion 10-year auction stopped at 4.683%, the highest yield since 2007 and just above the prevailing pre-auction level. The 2s10s curve stayed at 48 basis points, but 2s30s steepened 2 basis points to 104 as the long bond failed to participate. That resistance is consistent with the larger horizon: over 1 month, the 2-year yield is 1 basis point lower, while the 10- and 30-year yields are 12 and 18 basis points higher. CPI changed the near-term timing debate; it did not remove the compensation required for real-rate, deficit and buyer-base risk.

The main counterforce remains energy. WTI and Brent fell 0.90% and 0.66% on the day, yet were still 9.61% and 11.16% higher over 1 week, and the International Energy Agency estimated a 1.8 million-barrel-a-day supply shortfall this quarter, more than twice its earlier projection. Risk assets nevertheless treated CPI as permission to extend growth exposure, while credit markets combined broad access with severe issuer-level dispersion. Jane Street placed $14.6 billion of secured bonds, but Air Baltic and The Knot showed how quickly high financing costs and weak business models can transfer value away from creditors. The close therefore favors a narrow interpretation: near-term Fed pressure eased, but long-duration and lower-quality balance sheets remain exposed to oil, supply and refinancing risk.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

The rates move was concentrated in the policy-sensitive and intermediate sectors, though its small scale matters. At 4.20%, the 2-year yield returned close to its August 7 post-payroll level, yet the 5-year at 4.38% and 10-year at 4.68% remained above those closes. The 30-year did not rally at all. This was a confirmation of the front-end reprieve opened by July's 23,000 payroll decline and the 103,000 downward revision to the preceding 2 months, not a new regime in which weak labor has displaced inflation and supply as the dominant long-end constraints.

The CPI composition gave patient officials a credible reason to wait. Headline inflation rose 0.1% from June after a 0.4% decline, and the 3.4% annual rate eased 0.1 percentage point. Core inflation accelerated to 0.2% from 0.0% month on month, exactly matching consensus, while the annual core rate slowed to 2.5%, also in line with expectations and matching its slowest pace since March 2021. Energy fell 1.5%, and shelter rose only 0.1%, accounting for roughly two-thirds of the monthly headline increase. Lower hotel and motel prices helped restrain shelter, but both principal rent measures still rose 0.3%.

Underlying breadth was reassuring without being uniformly weak. Services excluding energy and rents rose 0.2% after declining in June, with medical care and airfares among the increases. Goods excluding food and energy rebounded after 2 months of declines. Computer software and accessories were 21.2% more expensive than a year earlier, a record increase, and other computer-related categories posted their strongest gains in more than 4 years amid the memory-chip shortage and data-center buildout. Those pockets do not overturn the aggregate slowdown, but they limit the inference that a single subdued headline has eliminated domestically generated or technology-linked pressure.

Household income adds a growth-sensitive qualification. Real average hourly earnings fell 0.2% from a year earlier in July, extending weak readings since the Iran conflict began. That helps explain why the same CPI report can lower immediate tightening risk even though headline inflation remains well above 2%: purchasing power is not reinforcing the price shock through stronger real wages. The Fed can weigh that softness alongside weaker hiring, but the three dissents at the July meeting and the persistence in rents leave the burden on subsequent data to remove, rather than merely postpone, the year-end increase priced by markets.

The inflation-linked close reflected this balance. The 10-year real yield fell 1 basis point to 2.42%, while the breakeven declined 1 basis point to 2.26%. Over 1 month, the real yield is 10 basis points higher and the breakeven only 2 basis points higher, so the dominant accumulated burden remains the real cost of capital and duration uncertainty. The day's equal contribution from real yields and inflation compensation contrasts with the prior session's breakeven-led rally and Monday's energy-led widening. Investors accepted that July CPI was not reaccelerating, but they retained a high real hurdle and only partially discounted the oil risk.

Curve structure makes the separation between policy timing and term compensation explicit. The 2s10s slope was unchanged at 48 basis points because both yields fell 2 basis points. The 2s30s slope widened to 104 basis points as the long bond held steady. Over 1 month those curves are 13 and 19 basis points steeper, respectively. The day's small movement in the front end does not look like a broad retreat from tightening; it looks like a redistribution of uncertainty away from September and toward later meetings, while the fiscal and inflation premium continues to accumulate with maturity.

The 10-year auction established the clearing price for that distinction. The $42 billion sale produced a 4.683% yield, the highest since the financial crisis and marginally above the level immediately before bidding. Demand was adequate enough to prevent a disorderly concession, but not strong enough to turn a soft CPI print into a sustained benchmark rally. A high auction yield can draw participation and still reveal that investors require unusually expensive financing terms from the sovereign. No inference about the next maturity follows automatically from the 10-year result; each point on the refunding calendar has a different duration and buyer-base burden.

Cash activity shows that the limited closing move occurred amid substantial risk transfer. Nominal-coupon trading reached $946.1 billion in original-face value, 19.7% more than the prior session. Activity rose 33.4% in maturities of 2 years or less and 30.9% in the 7- to 10-year sector, the two areas most directly exposed to the CPI repricing and the auction. Those totals do not identify customer direction, but they show that the modest yield changes were not artifacts of an inactive session. Policy relief and supply absorption were tested in size, and the market still closed with the long end resistant.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Credit carried the rates rally without displaying a generalized repricing of risk. LQD gained 0.12%, HYG rose 0.13%, and JNK added 0.17%. These are total-return gains consistent with slightly lower Treasury yields and firm risk appetite, not measures of cash-spread compression. The more informative split was between borrowers able to exchange size for a high absolute coupon and weaker companies seeking maturity relief on creditor-protective terms. Primary access remained broad, but the cost and loss allocation depended heavily on collateral, business durability and leverage.

Jane Street supplied the clearest absorption result. The market maker issued $14.6 billion of senior-secured notes: $5.86 billion due in 2031, $5.13 billion due in 2033 and $3.64 billion due in 2036. The longest tranche yielded 8.088%. Proceeds will refinance floating-rate loans within an $11 billion debt overhaul and support technology infrastructure and expansion of trading strategies. The transaction converted a large private financing discussion into fixed-rate public debt, but the yield shows the price required for that capacity despite record prior-year trading revenue of $39.6 billion.

Ratings capture the unusual mix of profitability and balance-sheet opacity. S&P assigned the bonds a BB rating, 2 notches below investment grade, while Fitch's issuer rating is BBB-, the lowest investment-grade tier. Secured status and the firm's earnings power supported exceptional size, yet investors still demanded an 8% handle for 10-year exposure. The outcome demonstrates that capital is available for strategically important technology spending and refinancing. It also shows that access at scale should not be confused with inexpensive funding, particularly when a closely held borrower is increasing leverage visibility through the public market.

Data-center financing remains a second source of concentrated supply. QTS subsidiaries began fixed-income investor calls for a potential offering of about $2.85 billion that could increase in size and is expected to carry an investment-grade rating. The financing is linked to a Blackstone-backed Georgia development leased to Microsoft, after an earlier potential bond-and-loan package of $5.4 billion and a $3.25 billion leveraged loan backed by Project Magnolia in July. The current step is investor engagement, not a completed sale. Its relevance lies in how rapidly recurring project, corporate and asset-backed channels are being used to fund the same infrastructure buildout.

Shanghai Electric showed a different form of market reopening. The city-backed equipment maker sold 1.5 billion yuan of 3-year green notes in the Shanghai free-trade zone at 1.8%, versus initial discussion around 2.4%. It was the first pricing by a nonfinancial company in that venue since authorities curtailed local-government borrowing in late 2023 and the issuer's first offshore sale since 2020. A Hong Kong subsidiary guarantee, a keepwell deed and an A3 rating helped produce the compression. The deal reopens controlled offshore-yuan access for higher-quality issuers while preserving barriers against the leverage that prompted the earlier clampdown.

At the stressed end, The Knot's amend-and-extend effort shows refinancing capacity becoming contingent on both price and leverage protections. The company launched a $670 million loan to extend an existing $660 million facility by 2.5 years, hours before Moody's cut it 2 notches to Caa1. The proposed spread is 525 basis points over the benchmark, up from 375 basis points, with an additional 100 basis points if leverage reaches at least 4 times EBITDA; that increment may be paid in kind. The existing loan had fallen to about 70 cents from roughly 99 late last year.

The Knot's operating deterioration explains those terms. Revenue fell 2% in 2025 and is expected to decline again in 2026, with margins remaining in the low-20% range as AI-generated search reduces traffic and vendor engagement. S&P retained a B rating but identified leverage above 7 times earnings as a downgrade risk. The financing therefore extends time without restoring the prior credit profile. A PIK feature at higher leverage protects near-term cash but can increase the eventual debt burden precisely when the underlying marketplace is losing relevance.

Air Baltic illustrates a more advanced transfer of value. Its €380 million senior-secured 2029 note traded as low as 12 cents on the euro after standing near 35 before the restructuring announcement, though the thin bond was also quoted in the low 20s. The airline plans to convert much of the note into equity, leave bondholders with €125 million of debt and raise €225 million of interim financing while shrinking its fleet and costs. A debt-service reserve held only €3 million as of June. Latvia owns 88.4% of the equity and 13% of the bonds, yet state ownership has not prevented secured creditors from facing deep impairment.

Taken together, these cases describe functioning but sharply tiered absorption. Jane Street obtained exceptional size at an exceptional yield; QTS is testing repeated infrastructure capacity; Shanghai Electric reopened a regulated funding lane with strong structural support. The Knot and Air Baltic are paying for time through higher spreads, PIK optionality, equitization and dilution. Benign broad returns can coexist with this dispersion because the market is still supplying capital. The dividing line is whether new money funds durable cash flow and collateral or merely postpones a capital-structure reckoning.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

Foreign duration did not provide a synchronized offset to the softer U.S. inflation print. Japan and Korea instead showed how energy exposure, domestic policy and buyer behavior can keep long yields elevated even when Treasury front-end pressure eases. The immediate implication for U.S. duration is competition rather than contagion: higher local yields give domestic institutions an alternative to dollar bonds, and currency defense can alter reserve-management incentives, while divergent inflation outcomes prevent a common global policy path.

The current Japanese delta is political as much as monetary. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has repeatedly treated tighter Bank of Japan policy as central to yen stabilization, whereas Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has resisted moving too quickly at the expense of growth. The BOJ has raised rates twice since she took office, but its policy rate remains 1%, and it held steady on the day of the joint U.S.-Japan yen intervention. With the currency again approaching 160 per dollar, intervention is losing force unless monetary policy and official signaling point in the same direction.

Expectations for a September or October BOJ increase reflect that constraint, but the administration's tolerance remains conditional. Takaichi's popularity has weakened as the cost of living has become more salient, BOJ officials have highlighted upside inflation risks, and cabinet members continue to endorse the central bank's independence. Bessent is due to meet Governor Kazuo Ueda around the end of August. A clearer alignment could reduce the need for repeated currency operations; continued tension would keep alive the risk that Japan must combine higher domestic yields with more active reserve management, raising the relative-value hurdle for Treasuries.

Korea supplied a realized long-end stress signal. Its 30-year government-bond yield reached 4.67%, the highest since the tenor was introduced in 2012. Elevated imported-energy costs and a senior Bank of Korea official's warning that semiconductor-led growth may require further tightening were already pressuring the curve; weak demand from life insurers added a distinct buyer-base problem. A possible reduction of ultra-long issuance to below 30% of next year's program could eventually change supply composition, but the current record yield shows that inflation and insufficient structural demand are clearing at a higher price today.

The oil shock also extends beyond central-bank rates. The IEA now estimates a 1.8 million-barrel-a-day global supply shortfall this quarter, more than double its earlier projection, with no durable Hormuz agreement in place. European power prices face additional pressure from heat-driven cooling demand and curbed French nuclear generation. In a conditional worst case where Hormuz remains effectively closed through year-end, internal U.K. Treasury modeling put 2026 growth at 0.9%, below the 1.1% forecast published in March. The scenario is not a realized growth result, but it captures the stagflationary fiscal risk: weaker activity and more expensive energy can coexist.

The net transmission to Treasuries remains asymmetric. Softer U.S. CPI can reduce the probability of an immediate Fed move, yet Japanese policy uncertainty, record Korean long yields and a larger global energy deficit continue to support term compensation. Foreign disinflation in selected economies may help their own front ends, but strategic dollar-duration demand must still compete with higher home-market yields and currency-management needs. That keeps the U.S. long end less responsive than the policy sector to one favorable inflation release.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Emerging-market assets did not receive a clean common-factor boost from CPI. The Dollar Index ended 0.11% higher at 99.932 after reversing its initial decline, and a developing-market currency gauge surrendered an intraday gain of as much as 0.2% to finish little changed in New York. EMB gained 0.12%, while a long-duration EM dollar sovereign index rose just 0.04%. The combination argues against a dollar-liquidity squeeze, but it also shows that a smaller September hike probability was insufficient to overwhelm oil exposure and local political risk.

Currency dispersion identified the relevant fault lines. The South African rand gained nearly 0.3% with support from precious metals, whereas the Brazilian real fell 0.3% and the Korean won lost 0.4%. The real has declined almost 2% in August as election risk entered pricing; the won reflected imported energy and the same long-end pressure visible in Korean government bonds. These moves occurred even as EM equities gained, so the distinction is not generic risk appetite. It is the distribution of commodity exposure, domestic policy credibility and prospective fiscal supply.

Indonesia sits on the resilience side, although the repair is incomplete. Its bond market has still lost 8.5% this year for dollar-based investors, the worst result in Asia, after concern over populist spending, central-bank independence and state intervention drove the rupiah to a record low. The nomination of Destry Damayanti as Bank Indonesia governor has restored some continuity, while the government plans to scale back its free-meals program and maintain this year's net bond-issuance target. S&P's affirmation of the sovereign rating and outlook adds institutional support.

The market response is measurable. Indonesia's benchmark 10-year yield has fallen about 27 basis points from its highest level since 2022, the latest debt auction drew the strongest bid-to-target ratio since February, and foreign funds were on course for a third consecutive month of net inflows. Those facts show that policy stabilization is attracting capital back. They do not close the fiscal question: the credibility of the next budget and the central bank's ability to support the currency without sacrificing its mandate remain the conditions separating a durable normalization from another oil-sensitive reversal.

Brazil occupies the vulnerability side despite one of the strongest currencies in EM over the full year. The real is still about 6% higher in 2026, supported by exceptionally high real rates, but election hedging remains light and local debt has shown rising yields and weaker demand at weekly Treasury auctions. Real yields on inflation-linked government bonds have climbed above 8%. The combination makes the carry unusually expensive for the sovereign balance sheet and leaves the currency exposed if investors demand protection before the October presidential election.

The new risk is not merely the identity of the eventual winner. Polling that strengthened President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's lead revived doubts about whether the next administration will deliver a primary surplus sufficient to stabilize debt. Local managers have expressed that concern through expectations for lower short rates and higher long rates, a curve expression of monetary relief colliding with fiscal pressure. Brazil's high nominal and real yields can attract capital for a long period, but weak auction demand shows that price-sensitive domestic buyers are already asking for compensation before the political outcome is known.

Corporate EM debt demonstrates why sovereign and company risk should remain separate. The yield on a broad EM dollar corporate index has fallen 19 basis points in August, versus only 2 basis points for U.S. corporates, taking its relative borrowing cost to the lowest since January. Oil producers benefiting from the Hormuz closure and distressed borrowers with restructuring progress led the move. China Vanke's 2027 bond returned 30% from the end of June after a ratings upgrade, while Gran Tierra Energy's 2031 note gained 18%. This is an energy and idiosyncratic-recovery trade, not a generic EM risk-on signal.

The broader conclusion is dispersion under stable dollar liquidity. Indonesia is earning back credibility through institutional continuity, fiscal restraint and stronger auction demand; Brazil is losing some of its carry premium to election and debt-sustainability risk; oil-linked EM companies are benefiting even as importing sovereigns face higher costs. A modest Treasury rally helps hard-currency valuations at the margin, but local policy and commodity incidence are doing more work than the common U.S. rate factor.

## Cross asset

Cross assets treated CPI as a near-term policy reprieve rather than a growth warning. The S&P 500 gained 0.26%, the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.74%, and semiconductors advanced 2.49%, while the VIX fell 4.78% to 14.55. The concentration in technology is consistent with the report's limited effect on expected activity and with continued enthusiasm for AI infrastructure. It also preserves the financial-conditions counterforce to Fed patience: risk assets strengthened even though the expected tightening cycle was delayed rather than removed.

Commodities complicated that benign interpretation. WTI closed at $82.45 and Brent at $88.32 after small daily declines, but their respective 1-week gains of 9.61% and 11.16% show that the physical shock has not normalized. Gold rose 2.52% to $4,493.60 even as the Dollar Index increased 0.11% and the 10-year real yield fell only 1 basis point. That combination points to continued demand for geopolitical and institutional protection alongside the equity rally, not a simple weaker-dollar response to easier Fed pricing.

Credit and EM complete the same mixed check. Small positive returns in investment grade, high yield and EMB are consistent with orderly markets and lower benchmark yields. The failed EM-currency rally, Air Baltic's collapse and The Knot's punitive refinancing terms show that abundant aggregate risk appetite is not suppressing every balance-sheet or policy distinction. Cross assets support the narrow front-end relief thesis, while oil, gold and issuer dispersion preserve the case for a high long-end and lower-quality risk premium.

## Forward Market Significance

July producer prices at 08:30 ET on August 13 are the next test of whether CPI relief extends into the categories that feed core PCE. Consensus calls for a 0.2% monthly increase after a 0.3% decline, with a 0.1% forecast also in circulation. A result near those rates, without broad service or trade-margin pressure, would strengthen the case that the Fed can wait for the next employment and CPI reports and would place the greatest response in 2- to 5-year yields. A broad upside result would expose how much of July CPI depended on falling energy and temporary category weakness, revive September sensitivity and push the adjustment through both real yields and inflation compensation. Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks later in August then determine whether the chair validates the market's shift from immediate action or preserves a deliberately wider range of policy outcomes.

The $25 billion 30-year Treasury auction on August 13 must clear a market that held the long yield at 5.24% despite softer CPI. The preceding 10-year sale stopped marginally above its pre-auction level at 4.683%, so the decisive observations are the long-bond result relative to its own when-issued yield, the distribution of demand and the stability of secondary trading after allocation. Broad nondealer participation and a contained post-auction move would show that current absolute yield can absorb duration even with deficits and foreign competition unresolved. A tail, heavier dealer retention or renewed steepening would reinforce the month's 18-basis-point rise in the 30-year yield and confirm that front-end policy relief cannot substitute for a higher fiscal clearing price.

Hormuz remains the test that links U.S. inflation, global duration and EM dispersion. Sustained vessel passage, accepted terms among the parties, lower freight and insurance friction, and crude holding below the August 12 closes would weaken the IEA's enlarged supply-shortfall path and reduce pressure on breakevens, Korean long bonds and oil-importing sovereigns. Continued closure or renewed enforcement incidents, especially with physical flows still impaired, would make July's 1.5% energy decline in CPI a backward-looking respite rather than a durable input to policy. The change in interpretation would be visible if oil again rises while breakevens and the 2-year yield move together; failure of that transmission would indicate that markets still regard the shock as acute but insufficiently broad to force the Fed's hand.

Fiscal supply, elevated real-rate compensation and a still-live energy shock left the close as a timing adjustment rather than a broad retreat from tightening risk.

Indonesia’s stabilization contrasted with Brazil’s election-linked debt concern, while energy exporters and idiosyncratic recoveries drove corporate strength.

section_summaries.market_read: Cross assets confirmed near-term relief, yet they did not validate a broad duration regime shift.

Oil’s weekly surge and gold’s strength preserved inflation and protection demand, showing that risk appetite had improved without erasing geopolitical or balance-sheet tail risks.

section_summaries.market_read: The next move depends on whether inflation, supply or energy becomes the dominant marginal force.

section_summaries.summary: Three near-term tests can separate temporary CPI relief from a durable shift: producer-price breadth, long-bond auction demand and Hormuz-linked energy transmission. Their outcomes will determine whether adjustment stays in policy-sensitive yields, spreads into term premium, or reopens inflation pressure across global duration and EM.
